Who assigned the main labels (those in labels_discrete_reported and dimensional_attributes): human / automatic / mixed / synthesis_specified (synthetic audio whose label is the emotion specified to the synthesiser)

Whether people checked the labels: human_reviewed (people reviewed automatic labels) / listener_validated (instructed labels confirmed or filtered by a listening test; the label stays the instructed one) / none (a source says there was no review) / unknown / NA (nothing to review)

How the audio was produced (;-separated): acted (acting, including film and drama performances) / elicited (emotion induced by stimuli or tasks) / spontaneous (natural speech) / read (reading without an emotion instruction) / synthetic (synthetic speech). The setting or medium is recording_context

How the main labels were made (;-separated): intended (emotion the speaker was told to portray) / perceived (emotion listeners perceived) / self_reported (the speaker's own report) / context_inferred (from the scene, script or meaning of the words) / automatic (a model's estimate). none = no emotion labels

Details of how labels were made: number of raters, what raters saw or heard (audio only / with video / transcript), how ratings were combined (majority, mean), which label set is the main one, listening-test details, etc.

How the spoken text relates to the emotion labels (;-separated when the data mixes designs): parallel (the same sentences in every emotion) / neutral_text (semantically neutral sentences) / emotion_specific_text (content matches the emotion) / unrelated_text (sentences assigned without regard to the emotion) / dialogue_script (lines of a film, drama or written dialogue) / unscripted (no script: conversations, broadcasts, improvisation)

Rights in the underlying audio, separate from license_spdx (which keeps the stated license): own / cleared / asserted / unaddressed / unknown. asserted, unaddressed and unknown mean the material needs a rights check. Empty = not examined
